lines: A dynamic stochastic oscillator after Xenakis: a waveform is drawn through a few breakpoints whose heights and spacings take a random walk each cycle, with a granulation stage and an FM stage on top
Sets the pitch of the stochastic waveform, from four octaves below C4 at the left to three above it at the right, with the result held between 1Hz and 3000Hz
Scales the voltage at the FREQ jack before it is added to the FREQ knob, from nothing at the left to the full amount at the right
Voltage over the pitch, a volt per octave at five times scale, so 5V is one octave; the knob beside it sets how much gets through
Sets how many breakpoints the waveform is drawn through, from 3 to 50; more breakpoints make a longer, less predictable shape
Scales the voltage at the BRKPTS jack before it is added to the BRKPTS knob, from nothing at the left to the full amount at the right
Voltage over the number of breakpoints, on a squared response so small voltages change little; the count moves in whole breakpoints only, because the total is truncated to an integer
Sets the largest jump the random walk may make to the spacing of a breakpoint on each cycle, from 0.01 at the left to 0.3 at the right
Scales the voltage at the DSTP jack before it is added to the DSTP knob, from nothing at the left to the full amount at the right
Voltage over the maximum duration step, on a squared response so small voltages change little
Sets the largest jump the random walk may make to the height of a breakpoint on each cycle, from 0.05 at the left to 0.3 at the right
Scales the voltage at the ASTP jack before it is added to the ASTP knob, from nothing at the left to the full amount at the right
Voltage over the maximum amplitude step, on a squared response so small voltages change little
Picks the probability distribution the random walk draws its steps from: linear in the down position, Cauchy in the middle, arcsine in the up position
Switches the FM stage on in the down position and off in the up position, which is the opposite way round from the maker's own description of it as an enable
In the up position a breakpoint that walks past its limit is reflected back; in the down position it wraps round to the other side
Sets the frequency of the sine wave that the stochastic waveform granulates, from six octaves below C4 at the left to three above it at the right
Scales the voltage at the GRAT jack before it is added to the GRAT knob, from nothing at the left to the full amount at the right
Voltage over the granulation frequency, a volt per octave at five times scale, so 5V is one octave
Sets the modulator frequency of the FM stage, in octaves either side of C4, and does nothing while the FM switch is up
Scales the voltage at the MOD F jack before it is added to the MOD F knob, from nothing at the left to the full amount at the right
Voltage over the FM modulator frequency, a volt per octave at five times scale, so 5V is one octave
Sets the modulation index of the FM stage, the depth of the modulation, and does nothing while the FM switch is up
Nothing in the module reads this knob. The voltage it scales is worked out and then thrown away, and the modulation index comes from the MOD I knob alone.
Nothing in the module reads this jack. Its voltage is scaled and added to a value that the module then overwrites with the MOD I knob's position, so patching it changes nothing.
Sets the carrier frequency of the FM stage, in octaves either side of C4, and does nothing while the FM switch is up
Steps through four grain envelopes: triangle at the lowest setting, then Hann, then Welch, then Tukey at the highest, which is where it starts
The oscillator's output at up to 5V, taken after a limiter that keeps it from clipping
The same signal as the OUT jack with its sign flipped
Note — A sine grain envelope is written into the module but cannot be chosen: it is the value below the ENV knob's lowest setting, so the knob cannot reach it.
Note — The BRKPTS knob is configured with a default below its own lowest value, so a freshly placed module has the count forced to the minimum of three rather than to the knob position shown.
Note — The plugin ships fifteen presets for this module, in the right-click menu's preset list: Abyss, Aftermath, Alarm, Drone, Emperor, Glass, Haunted, Interference and Noise Pollution.
Note — The rest of the shipped presets are Ocean Waves, Planes, Razor Blade, Rumble, Soothe and UFO Transmission.
Note — Both jacks are mono, and a polyphonic cable into any input is read on its first channel only.

ReGrandy.notes:
Several faults, all found in src/ReGrandy.cpp and src/ReGrandy.hpp at the shipped commit.

The MOD I CV path is dead. imod_sig is computed from the MOD I input and its attenuator at line 47, the MOD I knob is added to it at line 78, and line 83 then writes `go.i_mod = rescale(params[IMOD_PARAM].getValue(), 0.f, 1.f, MIN_I_MOD, MAX_I_MOD)` — reading the knob directly and discarding imod_sig. The jack and its attenuator therefore change nothing. The maker's API.md documents the input as "Modulates FM depth". Both controls are given lines saying so, because an untagged control falls back to the maker's tooltip, which is the text that has been proved false.

The FM switch is inverted. Line 74 reads `go.is_fm_on = !(params[FMTR_PARAM].getValue() > 0.0f)`, so FM is on when the switch is at 0 and off when it is at 1, while the maker's API.md calls the parameter "Enable/disable FM synthesis". The default value of 0 means a newly placed module has FM running.

The ENV knob is configured 1 to 4 against an EnvType enum whose first value, SIN, is 0. The sine envelope exists in src/utils/wavetable.hpp and no setting of the knob can select it.

BPTS_PARAM is configured with a minimum of 3, a maximum of 50 and a default of 0 (ReGrandy.hpp line 96) — a default outside the control's own range. Line 53 clamps to a floor of 2 rather than the configured 3, so the two figures disagree with each other as well as with the panel.

The FREQ knob is read twice for two different purposes: as the pitch at line 60, and again at line 67 as `go.freq_mul` through a rescale written for a -1 to 1 input. The knob's range is -4 to 3, and rescale does not clamp, so the multiplier runs well outside the 0.05 to 4.0 the constants name and goes negative below -1. The same shape appears at line 83, where a -4 to 4 knob is rescaled as though it ran 0 to 1. The lines describe what each knob is for and leave this arithmetic here.

ENVS_INPUT is configured (ReGrandy.hpp line 47) with no PortWidget in the widget constructor and no read in process. No cable can reach it, so it gets no tag and no line, and the jacks after it are numbered around the gap: the panel order left to right is inputs 0, 3, 2, 1 on the top row and 7, 5, 6 on the lower one.

TRIG_PARAM is declared in the enum, never passed to configParam, never given a ParamWidget and never read. It has no ParamQuantity at all. BLINK_LIGHT is declared and given no LightWidget and never written.

The panel and the maker's documentation use different names throughout. The panel prints BRKPTS, MOD F, MOD I, MOD C, MD, FM and MR; the README calls the same controls BPTS, FMOD, IMOD, FCAR, PDST, FMTR and MIRR. The lines follow the panel.

Every figure quoted in the lines is a literal in src/ReGrandy.cpp lines 6 to 21 or in the configParam calls: 1Hz and 3000Hz, 3 and 50 breakpoints, 0.05 to 0.3 amplitude step, 0.01 to 0.3 duration step, the -4 to 3 and -6 to 3 knob ranges, and the 5V output scale.
